Exponential pooling m=Σₖρᵏeₜ₋ₖ/Σₖρᵏ supplies a recency-weighted item-similarity signal; its effective horizon depends on ρ and history truncation. Adding g·LN(m) to SASRec does not establish separate long/short-term interests: [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781) already attends across history. Relevant precedents: [Fossil](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152), combining history similarity with sequential dynamics; [SLi-Rec](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/2019/0585.pdf), adaptively integrating long/short-term representations; [CLSR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13090), using separate encoders and contrastive proxy supervision to address entanglement. The residual is best interpreted initially as a recency-biased shortcut.

Algebraic implications of [LayerNorm](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.06450): LN(S/Z)≈LN(S) for positive Z, with equality ignoring epsilon. Thus weight-sum normalization largely disappears, while relative decay weights still change direction; pooled magnitude and associated confidence information are discarded. With affine LN and tied output embeddings, sⱼ=eⱼᵀ[h+g(γ⊙z+β)] includes g·eⱼᵀβ: a history-independent item offset for constant g, potentially absorbing popularity effects, though constrained by embedding geometry. For user-dependent g, the offset is user-scaled. If decay θ affects only this branch, ∂sⱼ/∂θ=g·eⱼᵀ∂LN(m)/∂θ; near-zero g attenuates decay learning. A sigmoid gate also adds saturation through g(1−g).

Ablate baseline, bias-only residual, pooling-only, and full model; uniform/last-item/fixed-decay/learned-decay pooling; no normalization versus non-affine/affine LN, isolating β; zero/small/nonzero gate initialization and fixed gates. Log gate values, decay gradients, effective horizons, branch score magnitudes and popularity correlations. Compare old-history versus recent-history interventions and report per-category plus macro validation HR@10 under identical candidates and budgets; gains alone cannot establish interest disentanglement.
